summary: Clean on the MEM dimension. The printf-family bindings hold no NRT refcounts, allocate no meminfo, and hand no @cfunc to a C library, so the classic numbox MEM hazards (refcount imbalance, @cfunc exception swallow/leak, cfunc-data lifetime) do not arise. The varargs ABI promotion, pointer-as-intp casts, snprintf size handling, and the pure-Python NUL-terminated buffer write are all bounded and correct on the supported 64-bit platforms. No findings.
